cita: Wang et al. (2026). E-mem: Multi-Agent Based Episodic Context Reconstruction for LLM Agent Memory.
problema: Prevalent memory preprocessing compresses complex sequential dependencies into rigid pre-defined structures (embeddings, graphs), causing 'destructive de-contextualization' that severs the logical/causal integrity needed for deep, long-horizon System-2 reasoning.
mecanismo: A master agent delegates to multiple SLM-based assistant agents, each holding an uncompressed raw episodic context segment (sliding-window chunks with overlap) plus a lightweight routing summary; a multi-pathway router (global narrative alignment, vector semantic association, BM25 symbolic trigger) activates relevant assistants, which re-experience and reason within their raw context to produce temporally-anchored evidence that the master aggregates and reconciles by timestamp.
evaluacion: Evaluated on LoCoMo and streaming HotpotQA (400/800/1600 documents) against Long-Context windowing, RAG, A-Mem, Mem0, MemoryOS, LightMem and GAM, with ablations on routing pathways, number of activated chunks, and master/assistant backbone scaling, plus a hallucination analysis on LoCoMo's adversarial subset.
numeros_clave: E-mem overall F1 54.17 (GPT-4o-mini) / 57.04 (Qwen2.5-14B) on LoCoMo, +8.86%/+6.63% over best baseline GAM (Table 1); Multi-hop F1 49.15 vs GAM 38.94 (Qwen); token cost reduced by over 70% vs baselines (abstract).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper's central claim -- that compressing history into embeddings/graphs is 'destructive de-contextualization' that loses provenance and sequential integrity -- and its measured gains from reconstructing raw context instead (Table 1) directly extend MF's fidelity/staleness concern with a concrete dual raw+summary architecture.

Reporting >70% token-cost reduction while preserving raw context via routed reconstruction (Sec 1, abstract) is a relevant cost data point, though not broken down per operation for MF's specific context-economy needs.

notes: Ablation on routing pathways and activated chunks in Fig. 3 / Sec 4.4; hallucination analysis Table 4 (Sec 4.3).

cita: Dong et al. (2026). KernelBlaster: Continual Cross-Task CUDA Optimization via Memory-Augmented In-Context Reinforcement Learning.
problema: Agentic CUDA-kernel optimization workflows typically treat each optimization task independently, so they cannot aggregate knowledge across tasks, causing biased sampling and forcing the agent to rediscover effective strategies from scratch for every new kernel or GPU generation.
mecanismo: A Memory-Augmented In-Context RL (MAIC-RL) loop treats the agent's Knowledge Base as its mutable 'policy parameters': a State Extractor derives a profiling-based performance signature per kernel, a State/Optimization Selector retrieves and weighted-samples (state, optimization, score) entries from a Persistent CUDA Knowledge Base, a Lowering Agent applies and profiles the change, and PolicyEvaluation/PerfGapAnalysis/ParameterUpdate agents write the resulting natural-language performance-gap analysis back into the Knowledge Base as a textual-gradient update.
evaluacion: Benchmarked on KernelBench Levels 1-3 against PyTorch eager mode, torch.compile, the IREE compiler, and the agentic AI CUDA Engineer baseline, using NCU-profiler cycle counts and application-level timing.
numeros_clave: geometric-mean speedups over the PyTorch baseline of 1.43x (KernelBench Level 1), 2.50x (Level 2), and 1.50x (Level 3) (abstract); motivating case: FlashAttention-2 ported to H100 dropped ~47% in performance before hardware-aware redesign (Sec 1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The PolicyEvaluation/PerfGapAnalysis/ParameterUpdate chain (Sec 3) explicitly consolidates raw trial-and-error experience -- successes AND failures -- into structured, reusable Knowledge-Base entries, a close technical-domain analogue to MF's promote-gotchas-to-durable-recipes consolidation pattern.

The framing of ICRL as far more sample-efficient than weight-updating RL or from-scratch search (Sec 2, In-Context RL discussion) is a relevant cost argument for MF's context-economy lens, though no direct token/dollar figures are reported for the memory operations themselves.

notes: Knowledge Base construction and consolidation loop in Sec 3 (Fig. 3-6); speedup results Sec 4 / abstract.

cita: Li et al. (2026). OpenSage: Self-programming Agent Generation Engine.
problema: Existing Agent Development Kits require humans to manually design agent topology, tools and memory, limiting the scalability and generalizability of constructed agents, and their static sub-agent structures discard informative states after each execution.
mecanismo: OpenSage gives the LLM itself tools to create/manage sub-agents (topology), write and register new tools, and read/write a hierarchical graph memory -- a Neo4j-backed short-term execution graph and a long-term project graph -- through a dedicated memory agent that supports both graph-based and embedding-similarity retrieval and can add, modify or delete nodes/edges, i.e. explicit write, consolidation and forgetting operations.
evaluacion: Evaluated on Terminal-Bench 2.0, CyberGym and SWE-Bench Pro (plus LoCoMo in an appendix) against agents built with SOTA ADKs (Google/OpenAI/Claude ADK, OpenHands, LangChain), with ablations isolating the contribution of agent-topology, tooling, and memory design (full agentic memory vs a Mem0-style graph vs no memory).
numeros_clave: SWE-Bench-Pro-Python resolved rate (Sec 4.4 memory ablation): full agentic memory 59.0% vs Mem0-graph 56.4% vs no-memory 56.2%; OpenSage vs the expert-designed Agentless baseline on the same 266-instance subset: 59.0% resolved (Sec 4.2); agent-topology ablation on a 300-instance CyberGym subset shows a large gap between the full configuration and NoFeature variants (Fig. 3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Sub-agent state, including 'resuming execution from a specific point in time' (Sec 3.4), is persisted as long-term/short-term graph memory that downstream sub-agents build upon -- a concrete pattern for treating in-flight task/plan state as first-class memory that MF could adopt.

The memory agent's search-then-add/modify/delete workflow over the long-term graph (Sec 3.4, 'so that only non-redundant, relevant knowledge is persisted') is a directly measured (Sec 4.4 ablation) consolidation mechanism MF's own consolidation lens could reuse.

notes: Memory-design ablation Sec 4.4 (Fig. 5); topology/tooling ablations Sec 4.2-4.3 (Fig. 3); plan_estado=SI reflects the resumable sub-agent execution state described in Sec 3.4.

cita: Hu et al. (2026). Pancake: Hierarchical Memory System for Multi-Agent LLM Serving.
problema: Existing vector-database memory backends assume static or batch-oriented indexes, so the highly dynamic, small-batch, interleaved search/insert/delete pattern of real agentic memory workloads makes approximate-nearest-neighbor search a dominant and growing share (up to 82-99%) of end-to-end serving cost as memory size grows.
mecanismo: A three-level (L0/L1/L2) cache-inspired index promotes and evicts vectors based on per-agent access patterns modeled as finite-state machines; a hybrid graph unifies multiple agents' coarse indexes into a single traversal instead of per-agent traversal, with per-cluster agent-specific access records for fine search; and GPU-CPU coordinated index management (insertion buffers, asynchronous transfers) lets hotspot clusters be updated and searched without full re-caching, all exposed via a Python API for scoped Insert/Update/Delete/Search across shared and per-agent memory partitions.
evaluacion: Throughput/latency benchmarks on realistic multi-agent workloads (compatible with Mem-GPT, LangChain, LlamaIndex), measuring end-to-end speedup and the share of total runtime spent on memory operations as memory size scales from 1K to 8M items, plus GPU-vs-CPU search microbenchmarks.
numeros_clave: over 4.29x average end-to-end throughput improvement vs existing memory libraries (abstract); memory-operation time share cut to an average of 3.2% at large scale, down from baselines reaching over 82-99% of total execution time (Sec 1); GPU vector search over 3x faster than CPU once cluster size >=512 vectors (Fig. 8).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Figures 1 and 8 directly measure memory-operation time as a share of total serving cost across memory sizes and hardware placements, hard evidence for MF's context/latency-economy lens that raw retrieval-index cost must be engineered, not assumed cheap.

Figure 2's multi-agent example explicitly Inserts/Deletes a shared task Plan object (P) as a first-class memory item across agent scopes, illustrating plan-state-as-memory, though the paper's own contribution and evaluation target index performance rather than plan semantics.

notes: plan_estado=SI corresponds to Fig. 2's Task-Planner-agent example (Insert(P,3) / Delete(P,2)); throughput numbers in abstract and Sec 1; scaling figures Sec 3.

cita: Mao et al. (2026). Joint Optimization of Multi-agent Memory System.
problema: Memory systems built as multi-agent construction+retrieval pipelines are usually optimized one agent at a time under a single shared global reward, which ignores inter-agent dependencies and co-adaptation and gives ambiguous credit assignment, limiting collaboration quality.
mecanismo: CoMAM models the extraction-agent -> profile-agent -> retrieval-agent memory pipeline as a sequential Markov Decision Process and jointly trains all agents end-to-end with GRPO, combining each agent's local task reward (evidence coverage, profile-quality score, retrieval precision/coverage) with an adaptively-weighted share of the shared global answer-correctness reward, where weights come from an NDCG-based consistency score between each agent's local-reward ranking and the global-reward ranking across sampled trajectories.
evaluacion: Evaluated on PersonaMem (32K/128K/1M context) and LongMemEval against no-memory (Base, RAG), prompt-based memory (CAM, MemoryBank, A-Mem) and RL-based memory baselines (Mem1, Memory-R1, GAM), with ablations removing each agent, disabling per-agent training, comparing single vs heterogeneous policies and independent vs end-to-end RL, and comparing credit-assignment schemes.
numeros_clave: PersonaMem accuracy gains of +8.5% (32K) to +16.7% (128K) over the best baseline (Table 1); LongMemEval F1 62.17 vs best baseline GAM 51.75 (Table 2); ablation (Table 3): removing any of the 3 agents drops accuracy from 0.64/0.70/0.66 (full) to as low as 0.51-0.57, and leaving one agent untrained costs 2-8% accuracy.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The per-agent ablation (Table 3) measures exactly how much each specialized construction agent (extraction, profile) contributes and how much its optimization matters, confirming MF's discipline of gating any consolidation-like role on measured, not assumed, contribution.

Retrieval-agent contribution and joint-vs-independent optimization of retrieval are directly ablated (Table 4-5) against downstream QA accuracy, aligning with MF's requirement that retrieval value be measured rather than assumed.

notes: Ablation tables 3-5 (Sec 5.3-5.5); main comparisons Table 1 (PersonaMem) and Table 2 (LongMemEval).

cita: Park (2026). Graph-Native Cognitive Memory for AI Agents: Formal Belief Revision Semantics for Versioned Memory Architectures.
problema: Agent-produced outputs (beliefs, code, documents, decisions) accumulate without systematic versioning or provenance tracking, so multi-agent pipelines lack a principled way to know which belief/output is current, why it changed, and what downstream conclusions depend on it.
mecanismo: Kumiho is a property-graph memory with immutable versioned revisions, mutable tag pointers, and typed dependency/provenance edges addressed via hierarchical URIs; updates are AGM-compliant belief-revision operators (e.g., a Supersedes edge creates a new revision rather than an in-place overwrite, satisfying Success/Consistency/Relevance while explicitly rejecting the Recovery postulate); an async consolidation pipeline (dual Redis working-memory + Neo4j long-term graph, hybrid full-text+vector retrieval) runs with published-item protection, circuit breakers and dry-run validation, and an AnalyzeImpact operation traverses typed edges to propagate belief changes to dependent conclusions.
evaluacion: Evaluated on LoCoMo (official token-F1 metric) and LoCoMo-Plus (Level-2 implicit-constraint recall) against Graphiti/Zep, Mem0, A-Mem, Letta, Hindsight and MAGMA, plus an automated AGM-compliance test suite (49 scenarios, 7 postulates) and ablations of consolidation enrichments (prospective indexing, event extraction) and answer-model cost/accuracy trade-offs.
numeros_clave: LoCoMo 0.447 four-category F1 (n=1540, highest reported on retrieval categories) with 97.5% adversarial refusal accuracy (n=446), overall F1 0.565 (n=1986); LoCoMo-Plus 93.3% judge accuracy (n=401) vs best published baseline Gemini-2.5-Pro 45.7%; prospective indexing + event extraction eliminated a >6-month recall-accuracy cliff (37.5% to 84.4%); 100% pass rate on the 49-scenario AGM-compliance suite; total run cost approx. $14 for 401 entries on GPT-4o-mini.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The near-perfect 97.5% adversarial refusal, explained as 'the memory graph contains no fabricated information, so there is nothing to hallucinate from' (abstract), is a measured instance of MF's provenance/staleness concern, confirming that versioned, provenance-tracked memory materially reduces hallucination risk versus flat overwrite.

The formal, AGM-grounded rejection of the Recovery postulate (Sec 7.3: a superseded belief is not silently recoverable, only reachable via explicit opt-in) is a concrete design MF's own derived-index-as-cache model could adopt when specifying what 'superseding a fact' must guarantee.

notes: Formal AGM correspondence and Recovery-postulate rejection in Sec 7; empirical results Sec 15.2-15.3, 15.7; architectural comparison Table 1.
